program_name: Texas Rural Hospital Debt Reduction Grant (HHSC RFA HHS0015180)
program_date_basis: RFA released 2025-03-24 (closed 2025-04-24), per HHSC's Rural Hospital Financial Assistance page
disqualifying_fact: HHSC: 'The 88th Texas Legislature appropriated $50 million to HHSC for the 2024-2025 biennium to establish grant programs for rural hospitals ... House Bill 1 ... Article II Rider 88 appropriated the grant funding.' STATE money, not RHTP. The dates close it independently: the RFA was released and closed in spring 2025, before OBBBA created RHTP and nine months before CMS issued Texas its RHTP Notice of Award on 2025-12-29. 21 RCJ Tier 3 candidates at $250,000 each.

program_name: Texas Rural Hospital Improvement Grant (HHSC RFA HHS0015677)
program_date_basis: RFA released 2025-03-11 (closed 2025-04-09), per HHSC's Rural Hospital Financial Assistance page
disqualifying_fact: The same appropriation and the same HHSC page as HHS0015180: 33 rural Texas hospitals at $350,000 each, funded by the 88th Texas Legislature's Rider 88 appropriation. RFA released 2025-03-11 and closed 2025-04-09, before RHTP existed. RCJ captured 32 of the 33 rows, which is a second, smaller §0.1 defect inside the first.

program_name: Texas ATLIS incentive payments to Medicaid managed care organizations
disqualifying_fact: Medicaid managed care incentive payments to Molina, Superior Health Plan, UnitedHealthcare Community Plan, Community First and Wellpoint. Not RHTP, not an award action in any tier, and not to hospitals. 5 RCJ Tier 3 candidates.

Medicaid IGT figures for the third payment of state fiscal year 2025. Not an RHTP award action in any tier. 4 RCJ Tier 3 candidates. The SFY 2025 designation is NOT used as the date -- a fiscal year is a period, not a date (see rhtp_resolve_action_date, REFUSED_FISCAL_YEAR); the disposition stands on what the document is.

program_name: Illinois HFS contract with MyOwnDoctor, LLC for Medicaid preventive care and education services
disqualifying_fact: A State of Illinois contract between the Department of Healthcare and Family Services and MyOwnDoctor, LLC for Illinois Medicaid Preventive Care and Education Organization Services, 2025-2026. Session 16 read it as 'a $1 2025 Medicaid contract that is not RHTP at all' -- and it is Illinois's ONLY RCJ Tier 3 candidate, which is why the survey ranked the state that awarded $50,008,264 near the bottom.

program_name: Nebraska Homeless Assistance Program (NHAP) Legal Services (DHHS RFA 4533)
program_date_basis: RFA released 2025-04-22 and applications closed 2025-05-21, both printed in the RFA itself
disqualifying_fact: Nebraska DHHS RFA 4533 says the department is "awarding state funds to an eligible and qualified agency to provide legal services" for the Nebraska Homeless Assistance Program, a HUD/ESG-linked homelessness programme ($15,000 over three years). STATE money, not RHTP. The dates close it independently: applications closed 2025-05-21, seven months before CMS issued Nebraska its RHTP Notice of Award on 2025-12-29. This is the programme behind RCJ's single Nebraska Lawyers Foundation Tier 3 candidate. THIS ROW MATCHES NO CANDIDATE TODAY AND THAT IS THE POINT OF IT. The sweep's provenance text is the source-document title plus the solicitation number, and RCJ's title for that row is the bare string "Intent to Award" with no programme identifier and no solicitation number at all -- so no source-scoped registry entry can reach it, and the date test cannot run either because RCJ carries no date for it (15 of Nebraska's 39 candidates are undatable). The automated sweep therefore caught ZERO Nebraska rows while a non-RHTP row was sitting in the candidate set; it was found by hand, by checking the name against the state's three notices of award. Nebraska's clean sweep line was a statement about the registry's coverage, not about Nebraska. The row is disposed of in ne_rcj_candidate_disposition.csv; this entry is kept so that the NEXT Nebraska candidate whose title does name NHAP or RFA 4533 is caught by machine rather than by luck.
